narratives.Overview:
1. Plain reads. `PLAIN_READ_BINS` gains `cut`, `tr`, `nl`, `jq`, `sort` and `sed`; `PLAIN_READ_GIT_SUBCOMMANDS` gains `grep`. Unsafe options: `sort`: `-o`, `--output`, `--compress-program`; `git grep`: `-o` (the text is lowercased, so `-O` is caught), `--open-files-in-pager`, `--textconv`; `rg`: `--pre`, `--hostname-bin`; `file`: `-c`, `--compile`; `less`: `-o`, `-k`, `--log-file`, `--lesskey-file`; `more`: `-o`. `sed` is a plain read only when every option word is exactly one of `-n`, `--quiet`, `--silent`, `-e`, `--expression`, `-r`, `-z`, `-u`, `-s` (any other spelling, abbreviation or attached value fails) and every script is a line-range print (`N`, `N,M`, `$` or `N,$`, then `p`).
2. One unsafe-option test, replacing the exact-word match in `usesUnsafeReadFlag` for every reader with unsafe options. It reads every word of the segment after the program name, a lone `--` and every word after it included. A short unsafe option `-x` matches any word that starts with a single `-` and holds the letter `x` anywhere after it. A long unsafe option `--name` matches any word that starts with `--` when the text after `--`, up to the first `=` if any, is a non-empty prefix of `name`. So `-o<file>`, `-uo<file>`, `--o=<file>`, `--o`, `--out` and `--output=<file>` all match.
2a. Trusted split only. The plain-read test runs only when every `;`, `&`, `|`, carriage return and line feed in the normalized text is also an unquoted, unescaped separator in the raw command. When any of those characters sits inside single quotes, double quotes or `$'...'`, follows a backslash, or comes from a `$'...'` or `\xHH` decode, no segment counts as a plain read and a mention is refused as today.
3. `xargs`. An `xargs` segment counts as a plain read only when every word between `xargs` and the program is on this closed list, matched exactly after normalization: `-0`, `--null`, `-r`, `--no-run-if-empty`, `-t`, `--verbose`, `-n` followed by a separate all-digit word, `-n` with all digits attached, `--max-args=` with all digits, and `--max-args` followed by a separate all-digit word. Any other word that starts with `-` before the program (another option, a cluster such as `-0r`, an abbreviation such as `--nu`, `--arg-file` or `-a`, or a lone `--`) means the segment is not a plain read. `XARGS_VALUE_OPTIONS` is replaced by this list; the guard never guesses whether an unknown option takes a value. Behind `xargs`, `sort`, `sed`, `git`, `file`, `less`, `more` and `rg` never count as plain reads; `cat`, `grep`, `head`, `cut`, `jq` and the other flag-free readers keep counting.
4. Heredoc data. In the mention test, the body of a quoted-delimiter heredoc is not a mention when all of these hold: its command is `cat` with exactly one `>` or `>>` redirect, or `tee` with an optional `-a` and one or more operands; every destination is a literal path (no `$`, backtick, glob character, `<(` or `>(`, and not `-`); no destination mentions the flag; and that command is the only command in the call (no pipe, no `;`, `&&`, `||`, `&` or newline-separated second command, and no `$(`, backtick, `<(` or `>(` outside the removed body). These checks read the raw call with the heredoc body removed; a quoted or escaped separator anywhere outside the body fails the rule. Otherwise the body is read as today. An unquoted heredoc body is always read as today.
5. Routing text. The kill-switch deny for a shell command adds one sentence: to edit a scratch file whose text names the flag, use the Edit or Write tool, which checks the target's name rather than its contents; other write checks still apply.
6. Docs. `content/docs/deft-directive-disable.md` (agent self-serve ban section) states the plain reads, the option test, the `xargs` rule, the heredoc rule and the Edit/Write route, each with its limit.
7. One PR, with tests beside `classify.ts`. No new verb, flag, policy field or stored file.

## In plain English
The kill-switch guard refuses shell commands whose text names the kill-switch flag file, so that an agent cannot create that file. It also refuses ordinary reads and data writes that only name the file, for example a `grep` piped into `sort`, or a comment body written to a scratch file. Agents working on any kill-switch issue hit this on every read.

The recommended fix counts a few more programs as plain reads when they carry none of their write or run options, and treats a quoted heredoc written to a literal scratch file as data. The design was audited twice on #6871. Each audit found one way to make an added reader write the flag file in one call: an output option with its value attached (`sort -o<flag>`), and an option whose value is a lone `--` (`sort -T -- -o<flag>`). This version closes both by reading every word of the command for unsafe options, with no stop at `--`. That refuses a few more harmless commands, and it must keep the protection: no plant of the flag file.

## Pains
- P1 — The kill-switch mention rule (#6681) refuses read-only and data-only commands that name the flag file: a read piped into `cut`, `sort` or `sed -n`, a `git grep`, and a quoted heredoc whose text is written as data to a scratch file.

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- The direct-write plant test (target basename only) and `decideShellWriteReissue` (every recognized shell write destination) are unchanged.
- polfer-owned surfaces (`docs/installer-refactor-ovpr/LLM-CONTEXT.md` section 5), including the AC9.12 entry guard for the disable flag: no change.
- The commit gate and the Write class (#6871), and the `session:start` lease (#6942).

A long unsafe option matches any word that starts with `--` followed by the option's first two letters, so `--out=<file>`, `--compress` and `--open` match. ## In plain English

The guard blocks useful reads and scratch-file writes because their text names the kill-switch file. Narrowing it is reasonable, but this mechanism cannot bind as written: a shorter `sort` option escapes R2, and a retained reader can execute a heredoc-written program.

Answers to the four Stop 1 questions:

1. **Yes.** `sort --o=.deft-directive-disable /dev/null` can create the flag while satisfying the proposed read classification.
2. **The option coverage is insufficient.** GNU `sort` accepts `--o` for `--output`. Beyond the seven newly considered programs, the retained `rg` entry lacks `--hostname-bin`, which runs a program. I found no additional missing write/run option for the other six named programs, but did not establish exhaustive GNU/BSD/Git-for-Windows version coverage.
3. **No additional lowercasing escape was established.** The two findings below do not depend on case. Scanning every word closes the earlier `-T --` boundary escape, but does not cure incomplete option recognition.
4. **No.** R4 can write executable content that a supposedly plain reader then runs in the same call.

R3’s exclusion of argument-sensitive programs behind `xargs` survives these counterexamples. R1–R2 and R4’s composition do not.

### 1. blocks-the-design — A one-letter long-option abbreviation escapes R2

**Pinned evidence:** At `838433b5b45bc24a1d28680fb136c9aacd874ccb`, `packages/core/src/authz/classify.ts:4276–4281` contains the option predicate R2 replaces; `4285–4319` admits commands when every segment qualifies as a plain read. `packages/core/src/hooks/shell-write-targets.ts:225–243` has no `sort` destination recognition.

Unexecuted counterexample:

```sh
sort --o=.deft-directive-disable /dev/null
```

GNU accepts unambiguous long-option abbreviations. In Coreutils 9.5, `output` is the only long option beginning with `o`, and `sort` uses `getopt_long`. Thus `--o` selects the output file. This follows from the [GNU abbreviation contract](https://www.gnu.org/s/coreutils/manual/html_node/Common-options.html) and [version-pinned sort source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/v9.5/src/sort.c), lines 514–546 and 4159–4160.

R2 rejects single-dash words containing `o`, and double-dash words starting with `--ou`; this word satisfies neither condition. Reading every word does not help. Empty input still permits creation of the output file.

**Disposition:** R2 cannot bind. Recognize every nonempty prefix of an unsafe long option, including one-letter prefixes, while retaining the all-words scan. Conservative over-refusal is consistent with the stated design. Add refusal cases for both `--o=<flag>` and `--o <flag>`.
